Query your REST API, access your database, and spin up test environments—all without leaving Claude. Learning Objectives - Understand Model Context Protocol (MCP) fundamentals - Connect Claude to WordPress REST API - Query WordPress database directly via MCP - Use InstaWP for instant test environments - Build custom MCP servers for WordPress Time Commitment - Exercise 1: 30 minutes (WordPress REST API MCP) - Exercise 2: 45 minutes (Database MCP Server) - Exercise 3: 30 minutes (InstaWP Integration) - Exercise 4: 30 minutes (Custom MCP Server) - Total: ~2 hours 15 minutes --- What is MCP? Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol that lets Claude connect to external systems like APIs, databases, and services. Instead of manually writing fetch calls or SQL queries, Claude can directly interact with your WordPress site. Benefits of MCP - Direct API Access: Query WordPress REST API without manual fetch calls - Database Queries: Run SQL queries directly on WordPress database - Real-Time Data: Always get current data, not stale snapshots - Test Environments: Spin up InstaWP sites on demand - Custom Tools: Build specialized MCP servers for your workflow --- Exercise 1: Connect WordPress REST API via MCP (30 min) Task: Connect Claude Code to your WordPress site's REST API using MCP transport. content: Week 9: Headless WordPress & Modern APIs Advanced Track - Optional Welcome to the Advanced Track! This week focuses on headless WordPress architecture, where WordPress serves as a content API while your frontend is built with modern JavaScript frameworks. Learn to decouple content management from presentation. Learning Objectives - Understand headless WordPress architecture patterns - Build secure custom REST API endpoints - Implement JWT authentication for APIs - Set up WPGraphQL and design efficient schemas - Integrate WordPress with Next.js frontend - Handle authentication and authorization in headless setups Time Commitment - Exercise 1: 45 minutes (Custom REST API Endpoints + JWT) - Exercise 2: 45 minutes (WPGraphQL Setup & Schema Design) - Exercise 3: 45 minutes (Next.js Frontend Integration) - Total: ~2 hours 15 minutes Prerequisites - Completion of Weeks 1-8 (Core Training) - Understanding of REST API concepts - Basic JavaScript/React knowledge - Node.js and npm installed --- Exercise 1: Custom REST API Endpoints with JWT Authentication (45 min) Task: Create secure custom REST API endpoints for a headless WordPress application with JWT token-based authentication. Context: When building headless WordPress, you'll need custom API endpoints that go beyond what the default REST API provides. JWT (JSON Web Tokens) provide secure, stateless authentication perfect for decoupled frontends. Requirements 1. Install JWT Authentication plugin 2. Configure JWT secret key 3. Create custom REST API endpoint 4. Implement JWT token validation 5. Add proper error handling and security 6. Context: GraphQL is an alternative to REST that allows clients to request exactly the data they need. WPGraphQL provides a powerful GraphQL API for WordPress with automatic schema generation. Requirements 1. Install and configure WPGraphQL 2. Expose custom post types to GraphQL 3. Create custom field groups for GraphQL 4. Write efficient GraphQL queries 5. Avoid N+1 query problems 6. Context: Next.js is the most popular framework for headless WordPress. ISR allows you to have static pages that automatically regenerate when content changes. Requirements 1. Comfort Level Check Rate your comfort with these Week 9 skills (1-10): - Custom REST API endpoints: ___ - JWT authentication: ___ - WPGraphQL schema design: ___ - Next.js integration with WordPress: ___ Real-World Applications When to Use Headless WordPress: - ✅ Marketing sites with complex frontend animations - ✅ Multi-platform content (web, mobile apps, digital signage) - ✅ High-traffic sites needing static generation - ✅ Teams with separate frontend/backend developers - ✅ Modern JavaScript framework requirements When NOT to Use Headless: - ❌ Simple blogs (traditional themes are faster to build) - ❌ Clients need to edit all content in WordPress - ❌ Limited development resources - ❌ No frontend JavaScript expertise on team What's Next? Week 10 Preview: Performance & Security Deep Dive - Diagnose and fix out-of-memory errors - Optimize N+1 database queries - Implement Redis object caching - Conduct comprehensive OWASP Top 10 security audits --- Headless WordPress Checklist Use this when building headless WordPress projects: API Setup - [ ] Install WPGraphQL or configure REST API - [ ] Set up JWT authentication - [ ] Create custom endpoints for app-specific data - [ ] Enable CORS for frontend domain - [ ] Test all endpoints with Postman/GraphiQL Security - [ ] JWT secret key configured - [ ] API rate limiting enabled - [ ] CORS restricted to frontend domain only - [ ] Capability checks on all custom endpoints - [ ] Input validation and sanitization Frontend Integration - [ ] Apollo Client or fetch configured - [ ] Error handling for API failures - [ ] Loading states for async data - [ ] ISR or SSG configured for static pages - [ ] Environment variables for API URL Performance - [ ] Query optimization (avoid N+1) - [ ] Image optimization with Next.js Image - [ ] Caching strategy implemented - [ ] CDN configured for static assets - [ ] Lighthouse score > 90 Deployment - [ ] WordPress backend deployed and accessible - [ ] Frontend deployed (Vercel/Netlify) - [ ] Environment variables configured - [ ] Custom domain configured - [ ] SSL certificates valid --- Resources Official Documentation - WPGraphQL Documentation - WordPress REST API Handbook - JWT Authentication for WP REST API - Next.js Documentation - Apollo Client Documentation Learning Resources - Headless WordPress with Next.js Course - WPGraphQL Recipes - Next.js ISR Guide Useful Plugins - WPGraphQL - Core GraphQL functionality - WPGraphQL for ACF - Expose ACF fields - WPGraphQL JWT Authentication - Secure authentication - Headless Mode - Disable frontend theme --- Troubleshooting Common Issues Issue: CORS Errors Problem: Frontend can't access WordPress API due to CORS policy. Solution: Issue: JWT Token Expired Problem: Authentication fails after token expires. Solution: Implement token refresh logic in your frontend: Issue: Slow GraphQL Queries Problem: Queries taking multiple seconds to complete. Solution: - Use query complexity analysis - Limit nested query depth - Implement query caching - Add pagination with reasonable limits --- Need Help? - Ask Claude to explain any headless WordPress concepts - Test all API endpoints before building frontend - Use GraphiQL IDE to explore your schema - Check Next.js deployment logs for build errors - Reference official WPGraphQL documentation Remember: Headless WordPress is powerful but complex. Start simple, test thoroughly, and scale gradually!
